correctness.rationale: By Alexander-dual definition, S is dual face precisely if EACH triple inside S induces a connected subgraph, not merely has an edge. For C_m square C_n, m,n≥5, induced triangles are two-edge paths, induced four-faces are precisely N coordinate squares, and no larger face exists by triangle-free minimum-degree bound. For each square, tetrahedron collapses across exclusive triangle, then another triangle across its exclusive diagonal; each straight 2-step path collapses across a free unique distance-two edge. This leaves exactly a triangulated torus plus L=N(N−13)/2 long edges independent of triangles, hence K ≃ T²∨(∨^L S¹). Integral Alexander duality yields H~_(N−5)=Z and H~_(N−4)=Z^(L+2), torsion-free and pure nonshellable. Independently enumerated 5x5,5x6,6x6 grids and executed all free-face collapses on 5x5 and 5x6.

originality.rationale: Published rectangular path-grid cut-complex results have disk cellulation and are shellable, unlike periodic torus. Published edge-disjoint-square criterion fails because each toroidal edge belongs to two squares. Resultary toroidal TOTAL two-cut is Alexander dual to clique graph, not ordinary three-cut; distinct degrees and functors. Robust clique forbids only independent triples, not all disconnected triples. No stronger theorem discovered that implies the torus fundamental class; unindexed equivalent hypergraph-complex formulation is possible.
residual_risks: Potential uncatalogued equivalent three-wise-connected hypergraph Alexander-dual theorem for toroidal graphs remains.
Family only m,n≥5; shorter cycles have extra short faces and were intentionally excluded.
